title: Graph search
statement: Start simple: Build an undirected graph. addEdge links two nodes in both directions and keeps neighbors in the order they were added. bfs and dfs return space-separated visit order, and each node is visited once. The theory is optional. The C solution appears after the hidden tests pass.
constraints: A node that was never added is still a valid search start.
think: Each node needs a list of neighbors.
An undirected edge is stored on both ends.
Breadth-first search takes a neighbor only after every node already in the queue.
Mark a node when you first discover it, before it is expanded.
hints: Use a queue for bfs and recursion, or a stack, for dfs.
addEdge must append to both neighbor lists.
A visited set stops a cycle from being walked twice.

tests.name: bfs-line
tests.call: { Graph g = new Graph(); g.addEdge(0,1); g.addEdge(1,2); return g.bfs(0); }

tests.name: branch-orders
tests.call: { Graph g = new Graph(); g.addEdge(0,1); g.addEdge(0,2); g.addEdge(1,3); return g.bfs(0) + "/" + g.dfs(0); }

tests.name: disconnected
tests.call: { Graph g = new Graph(); g.addEdge(0,1); g.addEdge(2,3); return g.bfs(0); }

tests.name: cycle
tests.call: { Graph g = new Graph(); g.addEdge(0,1); g.addEdge(1,2); g.addEdge(2,0); return g.bfs(0); }

tests.name: isolated
tests.call: { Graph g = new Graph(); return g.dfs(4); }

tests.name: duplicate-edge
tests.call: { Graph g = new Graph(); g.addEdge(0,1); g.addEdge(0,1); return g.bfs(0); }

objective: Visit each reachable graph node once while preserving traversal order and handling cycles.
workedExample: Start by marking the source visited before adding it to the frontier.
Remove one frontier node, visit each unvisited neighbor, and mark it immediately so cycles cannot enqueue it repeatedly.
recallPrompt: When should a graph node become visited: when discovered or when removed from the frontier?

misconceptions.explanation: Marking on removal allows the same node to be queued from multiple neighbors.
misconceptions.retry: Trace a two-node cycle and mark each node at discovery time.

misconceptions.explanation: Neighbor insertion order is part of this item contract, so the frontier must preserve it.
misconceptions.retry: List the neighbors as added and predict the next two visits.

reflectionPrompt: Compare the frontier data structures that make BFS and DFS differ.
